text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-The strongest earthquake since 1956 hit Lebanon: Two strong tremors and eight smaller ones hit Lebanon in nine hours. Some houses and cars were damaged. Thirty other earthquakes have hit Lebanon since 1982.
-A Lebanese-Syrian summit will be held today.
-The appointment of deans of faculties at the state-run Lebanese University caused a row between President Hrawi and Prime Minister Hariri.
-Parliament Speaker Berri meets French officials. Foreign Minister De Charette said: Running away from the land-for-peace formula leads to a deteriorating situation.
-Preparations underway for Hariri's planned visit to Russia on April 7.
-Former prime minister Hoss: I know from reliable sources that equipment for intercepting cellular telephone calls has recently been installed in Lebanon.
-Agriculture Minister Fakhoury bans the import of onions as of April 10 and imposes restrictions on the import of Jordanian tomatoes.
